newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: SKI JUMPING-GOLDBERGER DENIES NEW COCAINE ALLEGATIONS.
newsitem.headline: SKI JUMPING-GOLDBERGER DENIES NEW COCAINE ALLEGATIONS.

text.p: Austrian ski jumper Andreas Goldberger, who admitted to having tried cocaine once, on Wednesday denied new allegations he had often bought and consumed large amounts of the drug.
Current affairs magazine News reports in its Thursday issue that an arrested dealer admitted to selling cocaine to the former World Cup champion on three separate occasions.
"This is a lie," Goldberger told Austrian television ORF. "I tried cocaine once and never again had anything to do with the drug. I cannot say more than I already did on Sunday."

Goldberger, Austria's sportsman of the year in 1996, last Sunday admitted on television that he had tried cocaine just the one time at a Vienna disco last year and dismissed accusations of having bought and regularly consumed the drug.
However, the 25-year-old Goldberger did admit to knowing the dealer referred to in the magazine article, named only as Guenter Z.
News said the dealer claimed he provided the 1996 ski flying world champion with 20 grammes of the drug worth 26,000 Austrian schillings ($2,500).
The Austrian skiing association OeSV temporarily suspended Goldberger until the disciplinary board decides what action to take against him.
"We will not tolerate an athlete who takes drugs in the team. We have around 300 youngsters in the squad for whom Goldberger is an idol," OeSV spokesman Josef Schmidt said.
"The disciplinary board will decide Goldberger's future in about four weeks time. The punishment will depend on how often he took the drug but there certainly will be a punishment," he added.

Goldberger clinched the overall ski jumping and ski flying World Cup titles in 1995 and 1996. He has collected one gold, two silver and four bronze medals from world championships and Olympics over the past five years.
